brief: Goldman's sales and trading desk collects the charts its traders watched this week. It mostly reports rather than argues, but it states one thread and its offsets. AI infrastructure remains the main driver of EPS growth while absorbing an expanding share of the ten largest stocks' operating cash flows, so free cash flow yields compress. Physical AI extends that thread. Agentic task horizons double every 7 months, venture capital pivots to physical AI, and Goldman sees a 7% per year cost reduction in humanoid robots from scale and design optimization, pulling prototype-to-production forward. Against this the note sets three offsets. First, a stretched US consumer, where debt loads look manageable and credit card delinquencies plateaued but the savings rate is low versus the last 50 years and sub-prime auto delinquencies keep rising. Second, mutual funds' AI-exposed weight rose but failed to keep pace with benchmark weights. Third, a China semis value gap that may narrow next after the volume gap. Oil is a separate tail risk, with global inventories set to reach historic lows if the strait does not reopen soon. Goldman still expects gradual CNY strengthening.
